# Base image: Ubuntu 22.04 (arm64) with Flux, OpenMPI, and AWS EFA support pre-installed.
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package management to avoid prompts
ARG DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Set environment variables to point CMake to the MPI C and C++ compilers.
# This is crucial for building MPI-enabled applications.
ENV CC=mpicc
ENV CXX=mpicxx

# Update package lists and install necessary build tools.
# - build-essential: A meta-package that installs the GNU C/C++ compilers and related tools.
# - cmake: Required for Kripke's build system.
# - git: Required to clone the source code repository.
# - ca-certificates: Required for secure network communications (e.g., git clone).
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Clone the Kripke source code from the main branch into a temporary directory.
# Includes --recurse-submodules to fetch dependencies like the BLT build system.
RUN git clone --depth 1 --recurse-submodules https://github.com/LLNL/Kripke.git /opt/kripke-src

# Set the working directory to the source code for the build process
WORKDIR /opt/kripke-src

# Create a separate build directory for an out-of-source build
RUN mkdir build && cd build && \
    # Configure the build with CMake
    # - CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release: Optimizes the build for performance.
    # - ENABLE_MPI=ON: Explicitly enables MPI support, which is required.
    cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
          -DENABLE_MPI=ON \
          .. && \
    # Compile the application using all available CPU cores for a faster build
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    # FIX: Install the executable from the correct path ('kripke.exe' in the build dir) to '/usr/local/bin/kripke'.
    # This ensures the application is available on the system PATH with a standard name.
    install kripke.exe /usr/local/bin/kripke && \
    # Return to the root directory
    cd / && \
    # Clean up the source code to reduce the final image size
    rm -rf /opt/kripke-src

# Set the default working directory for when the container starts
WORKDIR /

  # Size specifies the number of pods in the MiniCluster.

  # Number of MPI tasks to run. Flux will launch this many tasks across the cluster.
  tasks: 1

      disable: true

updates.reason: The initial run was a single-task baseline (FOM: 4.37e-08). This attempt scales up to a full node (64 tasks on an m7g.16xlarge) to establish a strong single-node performance baseline before attempting multi-node scaling. The process grid is set to 4x4x4 to match the task count.

The previous run showed poor single-node scaling (FOM decreased from 4.37e-08 to 3.86e-09), indicating the default problem size is too small for 64 ranks. This attempt increases the problem size per rank using '--zones 32,32,32' and scales out to 2 nodes (128 tasks) to test multi-node performance with a more computationally intensive workload.

FOM has consistently decreased (4.3e-08 -> 3.8e-09 -> 1.0e-09), indicating severe communication overhead as the problem size per rank is too small. This attempt scales to the maximum 4 nodes (256 tasks) and drastically increases the problem size ('--zones 64,64,64') to give each rank more work, testing a weak-scaling scenario to improve the computation-to-communication ratio.

The Figure of Merit has consistently and significantly decreased with each attempt to scale up (from 4.37e-08 at 1 task to 1.03e-09 at 128 tasks). This indicates the default problem size does not benefit from parallelization. The single-task configuration remains the optimal one found.
